title: Unpaired Value
statement:
Find the one value that has no twin in an array where every other value appears exactly twice.

Contract
- `nums` has odd length of at least 1. Exactly one value appears once; every other value appears exactly twice, in any positions.
- Values may be negative, zero, or span the whole `int` range.
- Return the value that appears once. Do not modify `nums`.
- Use constant extra space; sorting a copy or counting in a map is allowed for correctness but not the intended solution.

Examples
- `[4, 9, 4, 7, 9]` returns `7`.
- `[42]` returns `42`.
- `[-5, 3, -5]` returns `3`.
hints: Think about an operation that makes a value cancel itself when it meets its twin.
Bitwise XOR of a number with itself is 0, XOR with 0 leaves a number unchanged, and XOR does not care about order.
XOR every element into one accumulator; paired values cancel and the unpaired one remains. Intended complexity: O(n) time with a single pass and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: the values separated by spaces or commas, every value twice except one, for example: 4 9 4 7 9
